subject.title: RFC: Standard Hosting Profiles and Ready Check

question: Should OpenClaw core own named, release-tested hosting profiles, and which minimal readiness contract should be accepted first?
rationale: The proposal creates permanent public configuration, probe, status, and release-conformance obligations that implementation quality or automated review cannot authorize.

options.title: Accept readiness foundation
options.body: Approve the condition model and default local projection first, requiring separate acceptance and live evidence for each non-local profile.

options.title: Accept all four profiles
options.body: Approve local, container, reverse-proxy, and node-mode together and own their stable selection, predicates, upgrade behavior, and release tests.

options.title: Keep checks host-owned
options.body: Decline core profile selection and continue exposing generic runtime facts for hosts and supervisors to validate externally.

recommendation.title: Accept readiness foundation
recommendation.body: Approve the condition model and default local projection first, requiring separate acceptance and live evidence for each non-local profile.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the existing Gateway readiness endpoints and has the strongest direct history on their current semantics and validation.
